bounded_statement: The report's headline claim (Welch two-sample t-test, t = 6.226, df = 46.0, p < 0.001, over 48 readings with 24 per liner) is not supported at the stated strength: only 12 independent units (tank_id) exist, six per liner group, and the 48 rows are four repeated depth samples per reservoir sharing the same liner_type. The supported bounded claim is that pooled per-sample chlorine readings averaged 0.200 mg/L higher in epoxy-lined reservoirs; any inferential test of the liner effect must operate on at most 6 independent reservoirs per group (e.g., tank-level means), not 24 rows per group, so the reported df = 46.0 and the associated p-value overstate the evidence.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the clustered sampling design (twelve reservoirs, four fixed port depths each) and states that each reading was entered as one observation, so the pooling is not concealed; however, disclosure does not make the row-independent t-test valid for repeated entries of the same reservoir.

[selected-result] Epoxy-lined reservoirs carried 0.200 mg/L more free chlorine than cement-mortar-lined reservoirs (two-sided Welch two-sample t-test over 48 readings, 24 per liner: t = 6.226, df = 46.0, p < 0.001).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the issue in three ways. (1) I checked whether analysis.py aggregates to the independent unit before testing (e.g., tank-level means, mixed model, or clustered errors): read_groups (lines 20-25) keys only on liner_type and never reads tank_id, and stats.ttest_ind at line 44 receives the raw 24-row arrays, so no aggregation exists. (2) I checked whether the data description could justify treating each row as independent: it instead names tank_id as the independent unit column (line 25) and states liner_type is fixed per reservoir (lines 15-17), ruling out row-level independence with respect to the tested factor. (3) I checked whether the reported statistics might actually reflect a tank-level analysis despite the wording: the report's own table shows 24 samples per group and df = 46.0, consistent only with the 48-row pooled test (a tank-level test would have at most df = 10), confirming the repeated entries drove the reported inference. All three attempts failed to overturn the finding.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py buckets every CSV row into the two liner groups keyed only by liner_type (read_groups appends float(record[VALUE_COL]) for each of the 48 rows, ignoring tank_id) and passes those arrays to scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a procedure whose validity requires each entered row to be an independent observation. Because each of the 12 reservoirs contributes four rows and liner_type is a fixed property of the reservoir, the same authorized independent unit (tank_id) is entered four times into a row-independent two-sample test, inflating the effective sample size from 12 tanks to 48 rows and the degrees of freedom to 46.
